description: Longitudinal wave speed in a long thin bar. The bar starts at rest; a short half-sine displacement push is prescribed at the x-min end face; the scorer times the first motion of the far-end particle set and divides travel distance by arrival time. output_fps is deliberately high (2000) because arrival detection at finite frame rates is the dominant error source.

pulse.formula: ux(t) = A * sin(pi * t / W) for 0 <= t <= W, else 0

regime_assumptions: thin bar: lateral dimensions (0.02 m) far smaller than the pulse wavelength (c * W ~ 0.045 m), so lateral surfaces relax freely and the 1D uniaxial-stress modulus E applies. The bulk P-wave speed sqrt(E (1 - nu) / ((1 + nu)(1 - 2 nu) rho)) would be the reference only if lateral strain were confined, which it is not in a thin free bar
linear elastic, small amplitude (0.1 percent of bar length)
provenance.notes: Tolerance is 15 percent, looser than A2, because first-arrival detection is coarse: the threshold crossing lags the true wavefront by the time the front needs to accumulate noise_floor_m of displacement, and the frame grid quantizes the crossing. output_fps = 2000 keeps the quantization under 1 percent of the travel time; the threshold lag justifies the remaining margin.
